Format-mismatch gallery ← back to the explainability dashboard 2026-07-26

The examples behind the fix

On MMAD's Discrimination subtask, Arm-C's original lettered-MCQ score docked it for 71 of its 400 answers because it replied in its own trained <answer>Yes/No</answer> schema instead of a letter. Every one of those 71 was graded wrong. But re-read in Arm-C's actual native format — the same image, the same model, just not forced through a letter — 51 of the 71 (71.8%) were actually correct. The other 20 were genuinely wrong even natively — shown here too, so this isn't a cherry-picked highlight reel.

51

20

This page shows a diverse curated sample of 29 (9 DS-MVTec, 20 VisA; 16 native-correct, 13 native-still-wrong) — not all 71, but spanning both benchmarks, both classes, and both outcomes so the picture stays honest. Full list: results/mmad_5subtask_eval/format_mismatch_examples.json.

Read before citing
  • All examples are Arm-C on the Discrimination subtask specifically — the one MMAD subtask that's genuinely binary and gets re-scored in this fix. Classification/Localization/Description/ Analysis are out of scope (see the dashboard's MMAD section for why).
  • "Original lettered-MCQ protocol" trace text is truncated to the first ~200 characters for display; the model's full <think> reasoning continues beyond what's shown.
  • The 20 "still wrong" cases are genuine misses, not a format artifact — the fix corrects the protocol, not the model's actual mistakes.
Source: results/mmad_5subtask_eval/format_mismatch_examples.json, armc_mmad_mcq.json, results_native/armc_discrimination_native.json — 2026-07-26.
